summary: Franklin County, Arkansas, site in the Ozark National Forest; OpenStreetMap maps an observation tower at 430 m, with no build date or present condition.

facts.status_note: No source confirms the tower still stands; the only tower record is an OpenStreetMap entry.

evidence.supports: Listed in Franklin County, Arkansas, within the Ozark National Forest
evidence.quote: Arkansas - Franklin County - Ozark National Forest

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap record name: Pine Mountain Lookout Tower
Preserve Arkansas: only about 40 of more than 120 documented lookouts remain standing
evidence.quote: Of the more than 120 documented fire lookouts in Arkansas, only about 40 remain standing.

evidence.supports: Preserve Arkansas: most of the state's towers are steel with metal cabs, prone to rust
evidence.quote: The majority of these towers are steel structures with metal lookout cabs, particularly susceptible to rust and deterioration.

evidence.supports: Encyclopedia: Arkansas had more than 120 fire towers at its height, 1930s to 1970s
evidence.quote: At the height of their use (1930s to 1970s), Arkansas had more than 120 fire towers
by 1994, forty-eight were still standing, and by 2023, there were forty-six

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Preserve Arkansas says only about 40 of the more than 120 documented lookouts remain standing, with no date given. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says 46 were standing in 2023. The story gives both figures and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Only two pages describe this site: a forest-lookout listing that gives county and forest only, and an OpenStreetMap record with coordinates, elevation and tags. Two searches and six page reads found no build date, staffing, fire or present-condition source. Brief kind (tower) and elevation (430 m) are supported. Status stays unknown, since an OSM tag does not show the tower still stands. The listing's '(Pinetree ?)' alias points to NHLR's Pinetree Lookout Tower (US 1695), which is in St. Francis County, so it was not used. A search snippet said the Ozark National Forest is now combined with the St. Francis National Forest; not fetched, not used.
